comment: Reviewed conditional branches that are neither loop back edges nor panic guards, per function (name without hash) and per target; see scripts/asm_check.py. 'max' is the ceiling per target; a target that is absent allows none. Entries were reviewed by reading the compare that feeds each branch (--show-other). A change in the count means the code generation changed and the entry needs a new review.

other_branches.reason: Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> drop: loop over the (public) vector length with a head/tail split; the bytes being wiped are never compared.

Sponge buffering: tests of the input and output lengths and of the byte position inside the rate (0x88 for SHAKE256, 0x68/0x48 for the SHA3 rates). Lengths are public in every call here (fixed per parameter set, or the ciphertext length). The permutation itself has no data-dependent branch. Unrolled byte-copy tails give the large counts; on i686 the length is spilled to the stack, so the compare reads memory.

Tests of the slice length (zero length, 4/8/32-byte vector-loop thresholds) and of the remainder after the vector loop (cmp len, done). The accumulated difference `diff` is only used by the final cset/neg/bif select: it never reaches a flag-setting instruction that feeds a branch. Read on aarch64 in full; the x86_64, i686 and armv7 listings show the same compare forms (counter or length against counter, length against immediate).

pykyber::mlkem::kem::decaps.reason: check_dk (FIPS 203 section 7.3) compares sha3_256(ek) with the h stored in dk. Both are derived from the public encapsulation key, so a variable-time compare reveals nothing about the secret part of dk. On armv7 the 32-byte compare of this one site is a bcmp call; the ciphertext comparison does not use it (it goes through reject_on_mismatch).
